Customer currently considers Hosted for pilots but has strong preference for Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem options) for production due to logging restrictions, encryption/KMS, and regulator (financial) constraints. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Vega (Redwood SE), Lisa Chen (Head of Data Governance, Eastport), Raj Singh (CTO), Marta Lopez (Compliance Lead), Tom Avery (Platform Engineer)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Carlos our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Lisa: Good thanks, Maya. Appreciate you fitting us in, we're trying to move pretty quickly on this evaluation.
[00:10] Raj: Morning—afternoon, yeah quick intro: I'm Raj, CTO, and we're evaluating options for hosting LLM features across our online banking channels.
[00:17] Marta: Marta from compliance, I'll focus on regs, especially around customer data and log retention.
[00:22] Tom: Tom, platform, I'll be hands-on for networking and KMS integration.
[00:25] Maya: Great. Quick agenda — understand Eastport's requirements around data residency and compliance, talk through Redwood's Hosted/Dedicated/Private options, and identify any blockers for pilot to prod.

[00:35] Carlos: A quick note — I'll cover technical constraints like VPC, KMS, audit logs, and how our runtime handles KV cache and prefix caching.

[00:42] Lisa: To start, our regulatory folks are clear: any PII or sensitive customer data must remain in-region. For EU customers it has to live inside EU data centers; for US customers it's fine in US. Also, we have strict restrictions on what can be logged — we cannot store full user inputs in logs for more than two weeks, and some transaction data must be redacted immediately.

[01:08] Maya: Understood. That's a pretty common pattern with banks. We support region pinned models on Hosted, Dedicated with reserved capacity in a particular region, and Private deployment if you need the control. For redaction and logging, we have configurable audit log policies and can disable request body retention on hosted if needed — though audit logs become more limited.

[01:30] Marta: Disabling request bodies is good, but we need cryptographic proof of deletion and KMS-based key control for any stored artifacts. Do you integrate with customer-managed KMS or HSMs?

[01:40] Carlos: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS — we have integrations with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and can talk about HSM for on-prem. Hosted customers can use our KMS, but for higher assurance Dedicated allows you to bring keys.

[01:53] Tom: For network isolation, how deterministic is the VPC peering? We need private endpoints, no egress to public internet for inference traffic, and full control over subnets and route tables.

[02:05] Carlos: For Private deployments we deploy into your VPC — that's our standard. For Dedicated we offer VPC connectors and private link options. Hosted uses regional tenancy and private endpoints for enterprise tiers but it's not full customer-hosted VPC. There are tradeoffs: Private gives you maximum isolation, Dedicated gives predictable throughput with more control over keys and logs, Hosted is fastest to get started.

[02:34] Raj: Latency is also a concern — some features are synchronous in mobile apps and need sub-300ms p95 for short prompts. How do Dedicated/Private compare to Hosted for latency?

[02:45] Carlos: Dedicated typically gives lower variance — you're not competing for GPU slots — so p95 is more predictable. Private can be slightly better if it's in your infra close to services, but that depends on your on-prem hardware. Hosted has regional endpoints with good latency but can spike under heavy demand. We use smart routing and fallback to smaller model variants to keep apps online.

[03:08] Lisa: On the privacy front, GDPR requires that logs and personal data be deletable on request. How do you handle deletion requests across caches and persistent logs?

[03:20] Maya: We have delete workflows; for Hosted we can purge stored inputs and embeddings upon request, but note that cache KV and transient runtime states may exist for short periods. For Dedicated/Private you have more direct control and can implement stricter retention by config. We'll document the deletion SLA.

[03:38] Marta: We need contractual language around data residency and processing - data not leaving region, subprocessors declared, breach notification timelines. Do you have a standard Data Processing Addendum?

[03:50] Maya: Yes we have a DPA and subprocessors list. I'll send the compliance pack after this call. For legal specifics we can follow up with our contracts team.

[03:58] Raj: One of our internal options is to keep embeddings on-prem and only call hosted models for generation. Any caveats?

[04:06] Carlos: That's feasible; you can store vectors in your own DB and only send masked context to Redwood. For scoring and embeddings we support self-hosted embeddings store patterns. Worth noting: sending masked context still requires careful PII handling in prompt engineering.

[04:25] Tom: About logging — can we set log redaction rules at the route level? For certain endpoints we want no logs, for others condensed stats only.

[04:33] Carlos: Yes, we have per-route logging controls and token-level scrubbing options. On Hosted we can configure retention windows and redaction rules, but Dedicated/Private gives you the finest control and local log sinks.

[04:48] Lisa: Auditability is critical — regulators want immutable audit logs. If we redact request bodies, auditors still need event traces showing actions but not the sensitive content. Does your audit trail include hashes or redaction markers?

[04:59] Carlos: We store structured audit events with hashes and metadata, so you can prove an action occurred without revealing PII. We can add HMAC'd pointers to full data if you manage keys.

[05:12] Maya: To be practical: for pilot we recommend Hosted in-region with strict retention and redaction, then for prod move to Dedicated or Private depending on your requirements for KMS and network isolation. That path usually balances speed and compliance.

[05:26] Raj: Cost will be a driver. What's the rough delta between Hosted at scale and Dedicated reserved capacity? Ballpark numbers are fine.

[05:33] Maya: Ballpark: Hosted per-token plus embedding pricing for intermittent usage; Dedicated is a committed monthly for GPU pools which lowers per-token costs but requires commit. For a mid-sized bank workload, Dedicated can be 30-50% cheaper at steady state with a 12-month commit. I'll send a more tailored estimate.

[05:50] Marta: Any certifications specific to financial services? SOC2 is fine, but we also want to see penetration test reports and evidence of secure development.

[05:58] Maya: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001. We can share a redacted pen test summary and our secure SDLC overview in the pack.

[06:10] Tom: Integration question — our SSO uses SAML 2.0 and we enforce SCIM for provisioning. Does Redwood support SCIM and SAML?

[06:18] Carlos: Yes, SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported. We'll need your IdP metadata. For Privates we integrate directly into your AuthN flow.

[06:27] Lisa: A potential blocker — our regulator asked that certain logs never leave our VPC. Hosted is likely out for those flows. How quickly can Dedicated be provisioned?

[06:36] Maya: Typical Dedicated provisioning is a few weeks once contract is signed and capacity reserved; Private can take longer depending on infra. For pilots, Hosted in-region with restrictive logging is fastest — but if regulator says no logs outside VPC then Dedicated with private link or Private is the path.

[06:52] Raj: We need a checklist of controls to run past our internal audit. Can you provide a mapping of Redwood controls to our requirements (e.g., PCI/FFIEC/GLBA relevant controls)?

[07:02] Maya: Absolutely. We'll include a controls mapping doc and an example architecture diagram for Dedicated and Private.

[07:10] Marta: About embeddings — retention of embeddings tied to customer identifiers is a no-go unless encrypted with our keys. Can we bring our own key and ensure that embeddings stored in your system are encrypted with that key?

[07:21] Carlos: For Dedicated/Private yes, you can bring your own KMS keys and we'll encrypt at rest with them. Hosted has bring-your-key via our enterprise mode for some customers — we'll outline the exact limitations in the pack.

[07:36] Tom: Also curious about model version pinning: we need to pin to a model version for reproducibility in audits. How do rollouts and pinning work?

[07:44] Carlos: Our platform supports model pinning per route and rollout policies like canary and A/B. You can lock a route to a specific version hash and we won't automatically upgrade it. That supports reproducible outputs for audits.

[07:56] Raj: If we go Dedicated, who manages OS patching and runtime updates? We want to avoid surprise changes during a compliance window.

[08:04] Maya: For Dedicated we manage the Redwood runtime and kernels; we coordinate maintenance windows. For Private options, if it's customer-hosted on-prem, you can control update cadence. We'll commit to maintenance windows in the SLA for Dedicated.

[08:18] Lisa: One more — breach notification. What's your timeline and are you able to support bank-specific contact channels?

[08:25] Maya: We have a 72-hour notification SLA for confirmed breaches and dedicated incident handlers for enterprise customers. We'll include contact and escalation paths in the materials.

[08:35] Marta: Ok that helps. For next steps, I'd like the compliance pack and then a technical deep dive. We'll also send over our standard vendor security questionnaire.

[08:45] Maya: Perfect. Recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO/HIPAA notes, controls mapping, redacted pen test summary, KMS and VPC architecture docs, and a Dedicated pricing ballpark. Carlos will schedule an architecture deep dive with Tom. You'll send the vendor questionnaire and any additional regulatory constraints.

[09:05] Raj: Timeline — we're aiming for a pilot in Q2 with production decision by end of Q3, contingent on legal and audit sign-off.

[09:13] Maya: Sounds good. Anything else from the group?

[09:16] Tom: No, that's it on my side.

[09:17] Lisa: Nothing further. Thanks.

[09:19] Maya: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and proposed times for the deep dive.

[09:25] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions of product names (e.g., "Red wood"), some timestamps approximate, and a few overlapping talk turns were merged.
